questions.title: Design a URL shortener
questions.prompt: Design a URL shortener. Start by clarifying requirements, then sketch the architecture in the design workspace.
questions.answerOutline: Clarify scale, estimate QPS and storage, choose base62 IDs or random codes, cache-aside for redirects, async click analytics, and rate limiting.
questions.rubricNotes: Score requirements gathering explicitly; it's half the signal at this level.

questions.title: Design a rate limiter
questions.prompt: Design a distributed rate limiter for a public API.
questions.answerOutline: Compare algorithms, choose a token bucket or sliding window counter in Redis with atomic scripts, discuss fail-open vs fail-closed, and headers.
commonMistakes: Per-instance counters without acknowledging the inaccuracy
questions.rubricNotes: Trade-off articulation matters more than picking the 'right' algorithm.

questions.title: Design a chat system
questions.prompt: Design a real-time chat application with history and presence.
questions.answerOutline: Gateways hold connections, pub/sub routes messages between them, persist-then-deliver, per-conversation sequence IDs, and heartbeats for presence.
commonMistakes: A single server holding all connections
questions.rubricNotes: Look for an explicit end-to-end message flow.

questions.title: Design payment processing
questions.prompt: Design a payment processing backend that integrates with an external provider.
questions.answerOutline: Idempotent create, explicit states, handling unknown outcomes, double-entry ledger, daily reconciliation, verified idempotent webhooks.
questions.rubricNotes: Correctness under failure is the core signal.
